content.comment_body: Hello all, I'm attempting to upload a project to a [product_name] device from my [product_name] software on Ethernet, but the software isn't detecting the device. I've tried multiple IP addresses, following a recommended "simple method" from another thread: open a blank network project, select 'Go Online', and the software should list [product_name] devices with their IP. Unfortunately, no devices appear. My setup includes: [article_no], [product_name] V[version_no], standard Ethernet cable, PC IP 192.168.0.1, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, and no gateway. Any suggestions would be appreciated.

The [product_name] with order number [article_no] is a version without display. For your software to communicate with it, you need [product_name] V[version_no]. You can update your software from V[version_no] to the latest version from [url]. Also, ensure your device firmware is up-to-date; if the version isn't [version_no], update that as well.
Thank you for your assistance. I have one more question: Can V[version_no] also be used to upload to [article_no]?
Yes, [product_name] software is backward compatible. V[version_no] supports all [product_name] devices.

Great, thanks! I believe that [article_no] also requires V[version_no], because I'm searching for this module and can't locate it. For the past several minutes I've been trying, and I noticed the 'Run/Stop' LED is showing red—is this expected?
In your original message, you only mentioned [product_name] V[version_no], not another version. Providing accurate details is essential, otherwise effective help can't be given.

I didn't give inaccurate info previously. I originally tried to connect to [article_no] and mentioned my connectivity issues. While waiting for advice, I found another [product_name]—this time [article_no]—and attempted the same steps with similar difficulties. Apologies if my troubleshooting caused any confusion.
Please verify that you've selected the correct network adapter—use the gear icon to check. If the wrong network interface is chosen, you won't connect with your [product_name] devices.

Hello again, I have a single network connection. Curiously, the PC IP shown is different from what's set in my computer, and I can't change it; on the device it's greyed out and locked, and when I try to modify on my PC, an error appears. ------------- EDIT 1 --------------- I upgraded the software to V[version_no], which revealed a new connection type. Only after this could I connect to the device and upload a basic program. However, when uploading a more complex project, another error appeared. Does anyone know what's wrong? ------------- EDIT 2 --------------- The problem was on my end—I neglected to add a Q output block. The [product_name] programming software blocks uploads if blocks are unconnected, which now makes sense. Thank you to anyone who assisted.

An update—it's no longer working. I managed two successful uploads, but now the device is running and refuses to reconnect. I haven't changed anything except trying to save a project originally built in V[version_no] within the newer software and upload it.
In the program you uploaded: Did you update the device settings from [product_name] V[version_no] to the newer version?

The issue was that a popup appeared asking if I wanted to overwrite the IP configuration. After confirming, my PC's gateway was changed, resulting in loss of connection and preventing further uploads. Thanks again for your help!

analysis.insight_summary: Users attempting to upload programs to [product_name] devices experience difficulties with connectivity and software/hardware compatibility via Ethernet. Issues arise from mismatched versions between programming software and device firmware, unclear error signals, and confusion over network configuration. Some program requirements—like mandatory output blocks—are only identified after failed upload attempts, causing frustration. Error messaging and feedback are often vague, delaying troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate [product_name] programming software to automatically detect and communicate reliably with all compatible devices, ensuring backward compatibility and providing clear instructions or error explanations when uploads or connections fail. They also expect helpful guidance when mandatory program elements are missing.
